arxiv-2011-10437.title: The effect of magnetic field on the damping of slow waves in the solar corona
arxiv-2011-10437.creator: T. J. Duckenfield, D. Y. Kolotkov, V. M. Nakariakov
arxiv-2011-10437.description: Abstract Context. Slow magnetoacoustic waves are routinely observed in astrophysical plasma systems such as the solar corona, and are usually seen to damp rapidly. As a slow wave propagates through a plasma, it modifies the equilibrium quantities of density, temperature, and magnetic field.

arxiv-2111-04024.title: Analytical impedance of oxygen transport in the channel and gas diffusion layer of a PEM fuel cell
arxiv-2111-04024.creator: Andrei Kulikovsky
arxiv-2111-04024.description: Abstract Analytical model for impedance of oxygen transport in the gas–diffusion layer (GDL) and cathode channel of a PEM fuel cell is developed. The model is based on transient oxygen mass conservation equations coupled to the proton current conservation equation in the catalyst layer.

arxiv-2202-04395.description: Abstract An article usually includes an abstract, a concise summary of the work covered at length in the main body of the article. It is used for secondary publications and for information retrieval purposes. The “lead paragraph” is encapsulated with the L a T e X quotation environment and is formatted as a single paragraph before the first section heading.

arxiv-2208-00771.title: 100 prisoners and a lightbulb – looking back
arxiv-2208-00771.creator: Vladan Majerech
arxiv-2208-00771.description: Abstract 100 prisoners and a light bulb is a long standing mathematical puzzle. The problem was studied mostly in 2002 [ 5 ] , 2003 [ 1 ] , and 2004 [ 3 ] . Solutions in published articles had average number of visits above 3850, but best solutions on forums had (declared) average number of visits around 3500.

arxiv-2410-00819.title: Absorbing State Phase Transitions and Stability of Long-Range Coherence in Dissipative Quantum State Preparation
arxiv-2410-00819.creator: Matthew Wampler, Nigel R. Cooper
arxiv-2410-00819.description: Abstract We investigate the absorbing state phase transition in a purely dissipative quantum reaction-diffusion model where the absorbing state itself has long range phase coherence. The model may also be viewed as a dissipative quantum state preparation procedure for the (generalized) W-state with errors.

arxiv-2509-21787.title: DeHate: A Stable Diffusion-based Multimodal Approach to Mitigate Hate Speech in Images
arxiv-2509-21787.creator: Dwip Dalal, Gautam Vashishtha, Anku Ranui, Aishwarya Reganti, Parth Patwa, Mohd Sarique, Chandan Gupta, Keshav Nath, Viswanatha Reddy, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Amitava Das, Amit Sheth, Asif Ekbal
arxiv-2509-21787.description: Abstract The rise in harmful online content not only distorts public discourse but also poses significant challenges to maintaining a healthy digital environment. In response to this, we introduce a multimodal dataset uniquely crafted for identifying hate in digital content.

pmc-10486641.title: Walnut Flour as an Ingredient for Producing Low-Carbohydrate Bread: Physicochemical, Sensory, and Spectroscopic Characteristics
pmc-10486641.creator: Monika Wójcik, Dariusz Dziki, Arkadiusz Matwijczuk, Urszula Gawlik-Dziki, Ana Belen Diaz, Cristina Lasanta
pmc-10486641.description: Walnut flour (WF) is a nutrient-rich source that can be used as an alternative for individuals on a gluten-free diet. This study aimed to assess the physical, chemical, and sensory changes in low-carbohydrate bread when supplemented with WF. Molecular-level changes were also examined using ATR-FTIR spectra.

pmc-10714632.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder among heart disease patients: a clinical follow-up of individuals with myocardial infarction in the Tromsø Study
pmc-10714632.creator: Geir Fagerjord Lorem, Eva T Næss, Maja-Lisa Løchen, Kjersti Lillevoll, Else-Marie Molund, Assami Rösner, Sigmund Lindkvist, Henrik Schirmer
pmc-10714632.description: BackgroundMyocardial infarction is likely to be experienced as a life-threatening and potentially traumatic event. Approximately one-third of patients with myocardial infarction experience clinically significant symptoms of anxiety/depression. However, it is unclear how many of these patients experience these symptoms because of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). We conducted a clinical screening of individuals with a confirmed myocardial infarction diagnosis.

pmc-10868366.title: Ventilatory Burden: Development of a New Approach to Better Quantify Obstructive Sleep Apnea Severity and Its Impacts
pmc-10868366.creator: Bastien Lechat, Danny J. Eckert
pmc-10868366.description: ease misclassification associated with current single-night diagnostic approaches (4–6). Techniques to identify different OSA endophenotypes to help increase success rates with existing therapies and develop new therapies that target specific pathophysiological causes have also been developed (7). In addition, new markers of OSA severity based on specific pathophysiological consequences of OSA have been established (8).

pmc-11492920.title: Factors Influencing Coping with Death Competence Among Chinese Oncology Nurses: A National Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11492920.creator: Youwen Gong, Yongyi Chen, Yang Liu
pmc-11492920.description: PurposeTo identify the factors affecting Chinese oncology nurses’ competency in coping with death, and their relationship with death attitudes and educational needs.MethodsA national cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted using an online survey of Chinese oncology nurses. Data were collected using the Coping with Death, Death Attitude Profile–Revised, and Death Education Needs Scales.

pmc-11516286.title: Future patterns of health inequalities in the population of England to 2040: a microsimulation study
pmc-11516286.creator: A Raymond, T Watt, H R Douglas, L Rachet-Jacquet, A Head, C Kypridemos
pmc-11516286.description: IntroductionThe existence of wide inequalities in health across England is well-documented. Our research adds to this evidence on inequalities in self-reported health by describing current patterns and projecting future patterns of inequality in diagnosed illness across multiple conditions by deprivation.MethodsWe used the IMPACTNCD microsimulation model that simulates a close-to-reality synthetic population of adults in England from 2019 to 2040.

pmc-11517014.title: Predictive machine learning algorithms for metabolic syndrome among Tunisian adults
pmc-11517014.creator: M Zribi, F Zaier, N Zoghlami, J Elati, P Traissac, H Aounallah-Skhiri
pmc-11517014.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMetabolic syndrome (MS), a cluster of interconnected risk factors for cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes, poses a significant health burden globally. In Tunisia, amidst an ongoing epidemiological transition, the prevalence of MS presents a growing concern. Our study aimed to identify the potential risk factors of MS and propose better machine learning (ML) based models for predicting MS among Tunisian adults.MethodsData was sourced from the Tunisian Health Examination Survey THES-2016, encompassing individuals aged 20 years and older.

pmc-11657914.title: Increased epicardial adipose tissue is associated with left ventricular reverse remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy
pmc-11657914.creator: Yuanwei Xu, Jiajun Guo, Yangjie Li, Shiqian Wang, Ke Wan, Weihao Li, Jie Wang, Ziqian Xu, Wei Cheng, Jiayu Sun, Qing Zhang, Yuchi Han, Yucheng Chen
pmc-11657914.description: BackgroundEpicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has been suggested to play paradoxical roles in patients with heart failure. The role of EAT in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patients remains unclear. We aimed to assess the associations between the dynamic changes EAT and left ventricular reverse remodeling (LVRR) in DCM patients based on baseline and follow-up CMR.

pmc-11734024.title: Overview of Effects of Motor Learning Strategies in Neurologic and Geriatric Populations: A Systematic Mapping Review
pmc-11734024.creator: Li-Juan Jie, Melanie Kleynen, Guus Rothuizen, Elmar Kal, Andreas Rothgangel, Susy Braun
pmc-11734024.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveTo provide a broad overview of the current state of research regarding the effects of 7 commonly used motor learning strategies to improve functional tasks within older neurologic and geriatric populations.Data SourcesPubMed, CINAHL, and Embase were searched.Study SelectionA systematic mapping review of randomized controlled trials was conducted regarding the effectiveness of 7 motor learning strategies—errorless learning, analogy learning, observational learning, trial-and-error learning, dual-task learning, discovery learning, and movement imagery—within the geriatric and neurologic population.Data ExtractionTwo thousand and ninety-nine articles were identified.

pmc-12483671.title: Baicalin alleviates oxidative stress in DF-1 cell line via the Mfn2/MAMs/Ca (2+) pathway
pmc-12483671.creator: Zhaoyan Lin, Jiao Wang, Junxin Li, Yu Zheng, Bohan Zheng, Qinjin Li, Xiaohong Huang
pmc-12483671.description: Oxidative stress is intricately associated with a variety of chicken diseases, and represents a significant challenge within the poultry industry. Baicalin (BA), a compound extracted from the plant Scutellaria Baicalensis, possesses potent antioxidant properties, however, the effects and mechanisms underlying the antioxidant activity of BA in chickens remain to be fully elucidated.

pmc-12502464.title: Opinion: Defining Readiness for Reconstructive Surgery in Patients With Advanced Pressure Ulcers—A Policy and Clinical Perspective
pmc-12502464.creator: Alica Hokynková, Petr Šín, Dimitri Beeckman, Vladimír Váňa, Hana Paulová, Andrea Pokorná

Even more concerning, long‐term follow‐up from a national database reported recurrence in 73.6% of patients [3].

pmc-12603822.title: Association of Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index with erectile dysfunction in the elderly population
pmc-12603822.creator: Biao Zhu, Tuanhong Xia, Li Li, Congling Mao, Le Kang, Zhaofa Yin
pmc-12603822.description: BackgroundThe Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) is a tool used to identify nutritional risk in older adults, but its relationship with erectile dysfunction (ED) has not been well studied. This study investigated whether lower GNRI values are associated with a higher risk of ED in older men using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).

pmc-12606748.title: Identification of Phenotypically Distinct Cancer Stem Cell Subpopulations in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
pmc-12606748.creator: Tarig Al-Hadi Osman, Oddveig Rikardsen, Muy-Teck Teh, Dipak Sapkota, Kristina Xiao Liang, Evelyn Neppelberg, Adrian Biddle, Ian Mackenzie, Lars Uhlin-Hansen, Anne Christine Johannessen, Daniela Elena Costea, Juan P Rodrigo
pmc-12606748.description: Simple SummaryCancer stem cells (CSCs) have been suggested to be the subset of cancer cells that drive tumor growth and progression and fuel the tumor with heterogeneous populations of cells, including those resistant to therapy. Different proteins have been proposed as biomarkers of CSCs in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC).

pmc-12664397.title: A multimodal dataset for human robot collaborative systems: Experimental data
pmc-12664397.creator: Shakra Mehak, Aayush Jain, John D. Kelleher, Michael Guilfoyle, Philip Long, Maria Chiara Leva
pmc-12664397.description: Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) systems are becoming increasingly integral to collaborative industrial and service environments. However, understanding human performance within such settings, particularly in Programming by Demonstration (PbD) frameworks, remains a challenge due to limited availability of comprehensive datasets. This study presents a multimodal dataset designed to assess human performance in HRI applications.

pmc-12718151.title: Impact of genomic sequencing information on physicians’ treatment recommendations for children with congenital heart disease
pmc-12718151.creator: Danton S Char, Natalie T Deuitch, Matthew K Berent, Wendy K Chung, Jon A Krosnick, David Magnus
pmc-12718151.description: PurposeGenomic sequencing (GS) is increasingly part of diagnostic evaluations of children with congenital heart disease (CHD). Past research suggests that clinicians might envision the most immediate benefits of GS to be guidance in decisions regarding withdrawal of care and rationing of scarce resources.

pmc-13682459.title: Rare common femoral vein adventitial cystic disease presenting with lower-extremity swelling
pmc-13682459.creator: Harsimran Panesar, Akmal Shahzad, Combiz Rezayat
pmc-13682459.description: Adventitial cystic disease (ACD) is a rare, nonatherosclerotic disorder caused by mucin-filled cysts within the vessel wall that produce luminal compression. Venous ACD is uncommon and may mimic deep vein thrombosis. A 24-year-old woman presented with right leg pain and swelling from a 2.8-cm common femoral vein cyst.
